notes: This is an Ollendorff Greek-Italian method: polytonic Greek exercises and Italian sentences, often printed side by side as parallel columns. Both the Greek and the Italian (with accents: fà, chè, poichè) read correctly (1-20, 33, 37-40), so the language and OOV flags reflect the bilingual genre. The Greek|Italian parallel lines (18, 21, 22, 24-26, 29, 32, 34, 35, 39) are labelled left-to-right exactly as printed, and the gutter rule will remove those it flags anyway. There are a few isolated faults: 30 has a doubled reading ('ἑσπέρας. ἑσπέρας. – Ὑπ Ὑπῆγεν'), and 31 and 36 are crops cutting through braces or two lines. Dropping C:repeated_word lines (2 in the book) is enough.
